title: Dog vs cat ownership
subject: pet
scope: What it costs to bring home and keep a pet in Singapore: setting up in year one, then food, medical care and insurance each year, with optional grooming and boarding. Adopted pets, HDB-approved breeds. Figures are mid-points of ranges published by Singapore sources in 2024 to 2026, not a quote.
limits: Emergency surgery (S$3,000 to 12,000), breeder prices and special diets are not included. Check licence fees with NParks.

extras.label: Optional services
extras.note: Monthly estimates. Frugal is 20% less, Comfortable 30% more.

items.name: Cat
items.notes: Start: adoption 150, sterilisation 250, microchip 70, vaccines 110, setup 170. Supplies: dry food about 80 and litter about 40 a month. Medical: booster 90, check-up 50, parasite control 100, insurance about 350 (S$210 to 640 quoted, Income and Etiqa 2026). About 15-year lifespan.

items.name: Small dog
items.notes: Start: adoption 400, sterilisation 450, microchip 70, vaccines 135, setup 250, puppy training 580. Supplies: food about 100 a month plus toys and gear. Medical: boosters 100, check-up 50, parasite control 120, insurance about 500, vet cab fares and licence.

items.name: Large dog
items.notes: Estimate scaled up from small-dog sources: larger food bill (about 180 a month), higher sterilisation and insurance (up to S$975 a year quoted for dogs). No Singapore source breaks costs down by dog size.
